t: Blogs - Import Blog Posts Using URL
html:
The URL Blog Importer in Eleva allows you to migrate blog posts from an external website without manually recreating each post. You can scan a source blog, review detected posts, and map content and metadata before importing. Posts with complete mapping can be published, while posts with incomplete mapping are saved as drafts. 


This article explains the URL import process and how to review the results.

What is Blog Post Importer?


The Blog Post Importer scans an external blog using its URL and detects available posts for migration into Eleva. It provides a guided process for reviewing content, mapping metadata, and importing selected posts.

Key Benefits of Blog Post Importer


The URL importer simplifies blog migration while allowing you to review content before importing it.


  • Guided import flow: Move through a clearer process from Scan to Review to Map to Import.

  • Better migration control: Review detected posts before importing them into your blog.

  • Manual metadata mapping: Add missing authors, categories, and tags during import.

  • Flexible import outcomes: Import both mapped and unmapped posts without being blocked.

  • Faster publishing readiness: Mapped posts can be imported as published posts, while unmapped posts are saved as drafts for follow-up.

Requirements for Importing Blog Posts


The importer uses information from your source website to find and process blog posts. Providing the correct URLs and platform helps Eleva identify the content.


You will need:


  • Blog Homepage URL: The URL of the existing blog.

  • Recent Post URL: A link to a recent post from the same blog.

  • Source Platform: The platform hosting your existing blog.

  • Destination Blog: An existing or newly created blog in Eleva.


Note: The source website must expose the blog post URLs for scanning. Posts that cannot be detected from the source may not be available for import.

How To Import Blog Posts Using URLs


The import process involves scanning the source blog, mapping its content, and selecting posts to import. Reviewing the detected content helps ensure posts are organized correctly in Eleva.


Step 1: Open Blog List


  1. Navigate to Sites > Blogs to see the Blog List.

  2. Click on an existing Blog or Create a Blog.


Step 2: Open Blog Post Importer


  1. Navigate to the Blog Post List of an existing or new Blog.

  2. Click on New Post > Import Blog Posts from URL.



Step 3: Start Importer


  1. Enter your Blog homepage URL.

  2. Add recent post URL.

  3. Choose your platform.

  4. Click Continue you will see that you have to wait for the mapping to complete.


Step 4: Map Contents


Import Time

Expect about 10-20 minutes for 1,000 posts.

Scan/Results Error

If the blog sitemap doesn't have a URL, then the blog posts cannot be imported. Currently you will see 'Scan in progress' for the interim 'Failure' state which upon clicking shows a blank page.


  1. Map Contents: follow the instructions to identify which elements on the page correspond to which pieces of information in your blog posts.

  2. You can see that all the mapping is done when all the checkmarks are green.



  3. When the import is done you will see X Number of posts were fetched on Date.



Step 5: Publish Posts


  1. Review imported posts in your blog:

    • Fully mapped posts are imported as Published.

    • Unmapped posts are imported as Draft.

  2. Select the Blog Post(s) you want to import.

  3. Click on Import Selected.

Troubleshooting Blog Import Issues


Import problems can occur when source URLs cannot be detected or content mapping is incomplete. Checking the source website and reviewing metadata can help identify the issue.


IssueRecommended Action
Blog posts are not detectedVerify the homepage and recent post URLs. Check that the source website exposes the required post URLs.
Missing authors, categories, or tagsComplete the available metadata mapping before importing.
Imported posts appear as draftsReview incomplete mappings and update the posts before publishing.
Import takes longer than expectedProcessing time varies depending on the source website and number of posts.

Frequently Asked Questions


Q: Do all imported blog posts stay in Draft status?
No. Mapped posts are imported as Published, while unmapped posts are imported as Draft.

Q: Can I import posts if some metadata is missing?
Yes. You can manually add or map missing authors, categories, and tags during the import process.

Q: What happens if some posts are mapped and others are not?
You can still import both types. Posts with completed mapping are imported as published posts, and posts with incomplete mapping are imported as drafts.

Q: How is SEO affected when importing a blog? Will SEO authority or rankings transfer automatically?
The importer migrates post content along with available SEO metadata, such as titles and descriptions. However, SEO authority does not automatically transfer simply by importing content. To preserve rankings and link equity, configure proper 301 redirects and keep the same domain and URL structure whenever possible. Without redirects, search engines may treat the imported posts as new pages.


Q: Do I need to manually recreate categories, authors, or tags after import?
Not always. If any of that metadata is missing during import, you can add or map it during the mapping stage.
